node-1.label: Patient developed left facial palsy with lagophthalmos and weak smile on smiling

node-2.label: A woman in her 70s presented with impacted cerumen in the right ear and underwent two attempts at bilateral irrigation by a practice nurse

node-3.label: Patient reported pain and hearing loss in the left ear immediately after syringing and subsequently developed purulent and blood-stained discharge in that ear

node-4.label: ENT examination found severe otitis externa with inflammation of the external auditory canal precluding tympanic membrane view; after removal of the wick, a small anteroinferior perforation of the tympanic membrane was visualized

node-5.label: Facial palsy was graded House-Brackman V, with good static tone of the mouth but weak movement on smiling

why.why: The new expert analyses reinforce that infection/inflammation is the most credible cause: the Laboratory Physician notes CT shows left middle ear/mastoid fluid without bone erosion and a normal external auditory canal, supporting otitis media/inflammation and making malignant otitis externa less likely, while the Radiologist also favors infection/inflammation over trauma or Bell's palsy. However, culture, inflammatory markers, and MRI remain pending, so confidence is raised from 0.85 to 0.88 rather than higher.

node-7.label: Facial palsy from iatrogenic syringing trauma

why.why: The expert analyses continue to favor infection/inflammation over iatrogenic trauma, noting no bone erosion on CT and prominent local inflammation; the Radiologist explicitly states trauma is less likely. This further lowers confidence from 0.1 to 0.08.

Both expert analyses refute an idiopathic cause, with the Radiologist stating Bell's palsy is less likely given the clear ear pathology and radiological/audiometric abnormalities. Confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.03.

node-9.label: Post-irrigation CT shows left middle ear/mastoid fluid without bone erosion

node-10.label: Audiogram confirms left mixed hearing loss with tympanic membrane perforation

node-11.label: Facial palsy due to middle ear/mastoid infection/inflammation

why.why: The Laboratory Physician specifically highlights CT findings of left middle ear and mastoid fluid without bone erosion as supporting otitis media/inflammation, and the audiometric mixed hearing loss with tympanic membrane perforation aligns with this cause. This direct expert corroboration raises confidence from 0.7 to 0.78, though MRI and culture results are still pending.

node-13.label: Ear discharge culture, inflammatory markers, and MRI with gadolinium are pending

node-14.label: Facial palsy due to acute bacterial otitis media with mastoiditis

why.why: Both expert analyses explicitly identify acute bacterial otitis media with mastoiditis as the leading cause. node-15.label: Facial palsy due to chronic suppurative otitis media with mastoiditis
